## Goal (user story)

As a developer/QA, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode (extending MainStreetMonteCarlo) that runs ≥200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics, so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.

## Context

`MainStreetMonteCarlo` is single-player only (`runMonteCarlo` / `runAllCombinations` with one strategy × one difficulty per run). Competitive mode needs head-to-head metrics: both players' win/score distributions plus per-player diagnostics. Architecture is N-player-ready (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner), but the harness validates the head-to-head (human vs 1 AI) path initially; N>2 extension is a future parameterisation.

## Scope

- Head-to-head harness extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (new entry point or flag): both players act per shared-day, same seed → deterministic head-to-head run.
- ≥200 seeds; outputs win/score distributions plus per-player metrics (wins per owner, average score per owner, draw/early-end handling).
- Single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

## Out of scope

- AI strategy itself (sibling).
- Per-owner income routing (sibling).
- Rendering / scene (AC5 child).
- Endless continuation (deferred).
- N>2 Monte Carlo — harness is N-player-extensible (numOpponents param) but AC4 validates head-to-head; broader N is a follow-up.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Head-to-head harness runs ≥200 seeds with deterministic head-to-head execution (same seed → same per-owner outcome) and produces win/score distributions (win rate per owner, median/average score per owner).
- [ ] **AC2:** Per-player metrics include at least wins, average score, and loss-reason distribution per owner plus a deterministic summary (draw/early-end handling documented).
- [ ] **AC3:** Extension of `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (not a replacement); existing `runMonteCarlo` / `runAllCombinations` and `monte-carlo-balance.test.ts` still pass.
- [ ] **AC4:** Validated against the adapted competitive AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038).

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness extension (win/score distributions, per-player metrics).
- `tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive Monte Carlo tests (determinism, distributions, guardrails).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30
- Depends on: competitive state model + phase machine + income routing + AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038)
- Architecture: N-player-ready state/phase; harness parametrises head-to-head initially

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the shared street rendered with owner-coloured slots, shared-market phase alternation, and SFX/animations (per AGENTS.md §8), so competitive ownership is visually and audibly unambiguous.

## Context

AC5 of the parent epic is engine-only: no game-selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome. This planning-created child (per AC5 “deferred to a planning child” and producer Q2 “planning”) captures the deferred rendering scope for the next milestone. Worker must use core-engine animation helpers with `soundManager` + `sfx` (AGENTS.md §8: every animated action needs sound + animation; SFX keys via `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, no literals).

## Scope

- Competitive scene (Phaser scene) with SLL layout.
- Owner-coloured street: each placed business's street slot tinted by owner (e.g. player = blue, AI = red) so the shared grid's ownership is immediately readable.
- Shared-market phase alternation: alternate MarketPhases within a shared day with visible whose-turn affordance.
- SFX/animations for all competitive actions (deal/flip/place/discard/illegal) via helpers + `SoundManager`, respecting reduced-motion and mute.
- Turn alternation SFX/animation sequencing so AI actions are visible (delayed AI turn like Coloretto precedent).

## Out of scope

- Engine state/phase/income/AI/Monte Carlo (parent epic siblings).
- Game-selector entry — include only when the scene is ready for play (within this child).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Competitive scene renders the shared street with per-slot owner colour (player vs AI unambiguously distinct); SLL layout used (no hardcoded pixel positions).
- [ ] **AC2:** Shared-market phase alternation is visible (whose turn) and input is gated to the active player; AI turn is animated with a brief delay.
- [ ] **AC3:** Every competitive action that uses a core-engine animation helper is wired with SFX (via helper `soundManager`/`sfx` params or `GameEventEmitter`/`SoundManager`); SFX keys follow `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` convention; reduced-motion and mute respected.
- [ ] **AC4:** Build + unit tests pass; smoke browser coverage for the scene.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScene.ts` — Competitive scene (owner-coloured street, phase alternation, SFX).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveRenderer.ts` — Owner-colour helpers (tinting by ownerId).
- `src/core-engine/SoundManager.ts` — `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` source of truth for SFX keys.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-scene.browser.test.ts` — Smoke/browser coverage.

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 — Main Street competitive mode (engine-only; rendering deferred here per AC5)
- Siblings: state, phase, income/events, AI strategy, Monte Carlo (engine foundation this child renders)
- AGENTS.md §8 — Every action with animation must have SFX

# Add images for all cards

## Problem Statement

The Main Street card redesign (CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN) reserves a 64×64 left-art graphic zone on every card face, but all 162 cards currently display only a placeholder (synergy-coloured rectangle with a single-letter initial). Images must be generated from the `art_notes` descriptions in `card-data.csv`, packaged as PNGs, and embedded into the SVG card rendering pipeline so they appear alongside the card text.

## Users

- **Players**: See distinctive, thematic imagery on every card face in their hand, on the street, and in the market — improving recognisability and atmosphere.
- **Developers**: Have a reproducible image-generation pipeline that produces one PNG per card from `art_notes`, with a safe fallback to a generic placeholder when no image exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every card across all families (business, community-space, event, upgrade, staff) has an associated 64×64 PNG image file in `public/assets/games/main-street/cards/`.
2. Images are named `<card_id>_64_x_64.png` (e.g. `biz-bakery_64_x_64.png`) and are referenced by the SVG card generator, which attempts to embed the corresponding PNG and falls back to a generic placeholder when the file is missing.
3. The `graphicZoneSvg()` function in `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` is updated to embed `<image>` elements for the PNG assets (with a fallback `<rect>` + glyph when the image is unavailable or fails to load).
4. All 162 card entries in `card-data.csv` have an `art_notes` value — cards that previously had none receive a generic placeholder description.
5. The full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Risks & Mitigations

- **Image generation quality**: AI-generated images may not match the intended aesthetic. Mitigation: producer reviews images before committing to the repo; a script to regenerate is preferred over manual editing.
- **SVG `<image>` fallback reliability**: SVG `<image>` elements do not gracefully handle missing files — the zone may render blank. Mitigation: the SVG generator emits the `<image>` element, and when the file is absent, falls back to the existing `<rect>` + glyph placeholder.
- **Licensing**: Generated images must be clearly documented as CC0 / self-authored. Mitigation: update `CREDITS.md` with provenance for every new asset directory.
- **Scope creep**: "Every card" could imply artwork for other example games (Golf, Lost Cities, etc.). Mitigation: scope is strictly Main Street 162 cards.

## Constraints

- Images must be permissive / freely available for commercial use (CC0, MIT, or self-authored).
- The naming convention must be deterministic from the card id so the SVG generator can derive asset keys at runtime without additional configuration.
- SVG `<image>` elements must have proper fallback handling so missing assets do not break rendering.
- The 64×64 zone is at `(8, 8)` on the 140×80 card canvas, so images must fit within that rect.

## Existing State

- `public/assets/cards/` — 52 standard playing-card SVGs (CC0, saulspatz/SVGCards) + 1 card back.
- `public/assets/cards/alternative/webisso/` — 52 playing-card SVGs (MIT).
- `public/assets/cards/lost-cities/` — 61 Lost Cities SVGs (MIT).
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — 162 rows; 157 have `art_notes`, 5 are empty.
- `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — `graphicZoneSvg()` produces a coloured rectangle + initial glyph; comment notes: "Future work can replace the `<g>` body with a real `<image>` or family-specific icon."
- No 64×64 card art images exist anywhere in the project.

## Desired Change

1. Populate `art_notes` for the 5 cards that currently have none (use a generic placeholder description).
2. Generate 64×64 PNG images for all 162 cards from their `art_notes` descriptions, naming them `<card_id>_64_x_64.png` (e.g. `biz-bakery_64_x_64.png`, `comm-library_64_x_64.png`).
3. Place images in `public/assets/games/main-street/cards/`.
4. Update `graphicZoneSvg()` to optionally embed an `<image href="...">` element inside the 64×64 zone, with a `<rect>` + glyph fallback.
5. Update the SVG generation pipeline so the asset key is derived from the card id at runtime.

## Key Files (delivered layout, verified 2026-09-29)

- `src/card-data.csv` — card rows; all 173 rows carry an `art_notes` value
- `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` — producer-supplied source art (1024×1024)
- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` — builds the art map from the CSV and sprites
- `src/card-art-map.json` — generated card-name → embedded 256×256 WebP `data:` URI map
- `src/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — runtime resolver (`getCardArtDataUri`, `resolveCardArtName`, `hasDedicatedCardArt`)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — `graphicZoneSvg()` embeds the clipped `<image>` with a `<rect>` + glyph fallback
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — pending-aware drift guard (`PENDING_ART_TARGETS`, baseline 78)
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — artifact provenance to update when the new sprites land

## Related Work

- **CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN** — Redesign all Main Street cards with 64×64 left-art (created the placeholder zone).
- **CG-0MMJTGQFE1RL6VJA** — Add synergy icons to Main Street help panel (complementary asset work).
- **CG-0MM4RF91E1LR5RSY** — Main Street: PRD Milestone 4 — Visual Polish, Animation, and Audio (mentions placeholder-to-final art pipeline).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: Image format? — **Answer (producer):** PNG files.
- Q: How will images be created and named? — **Answer (producer):** Producer will provide images; naming convention `<card_name>_64_x_64.png`, derived from card id. Placeholder used if image not found.
- Q: Scope — all card families? — **Answer (producer):** Every family (business, community-space, event, upgrade, staff).
- Q: Placement approach — SVG or external Phaser assets? — **Answer (producer):** Embedded in SVG.
- Q: Cards without art_notes (5 cards)? — **Answer (producer):** Create art_notes; use a placeholder description.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MLULUJFI0UNA47U** – Extend GameEventEmitter with solitaire events (completed)
- **CG-0MQ7G3DTJ0082CGR** – Sushi Go: Partial HandView migration (layout only) (completed)
- **CG-0MM4RDYAU1DY4OG8** – Main Street: PRD Milestone 1 -- Playable Core Loop (Walking Skeleton) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: absent, accept, acceptance, add, additional (+194 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: accept, acceptance, add, additional, alternative (+154 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: accept, add, alternative, animation, appear (+132 more)


## Plan reconciliation (plan session 2026-09-29)

The card-art mechanism this item originally specified is **already delivered**
under related work items, using a producer-approved architecture that differs
from the original “64×64 PNG in `public/assets/...`” wording:

| Original wording | Delivered implementation | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 64×64 PNG per card in `public/assets/games/main-street/cards/<card_id>_64_x_64.png` | 1024×1024 source sprites in `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, embedded as 256×256 WebP `data:` URIs generated from `src/card-art-map.json` | Producer decision Q4 (MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E); `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` |
| `graphicZoneSvg()` embeds `<image>` + fallback | Done — `graphicZoneSvg()` accepts an art data URI and emits a clipped `<image>`, falling back to `<rect>` + glyph | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` |
| All cards have `art_notes` | Done — 173/173 rows in `src/card-data.csv` carry `art_notes` | verified 2026-09-29 |
| Naming `<card_id>_64_x_64.png` | Superseded — `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; the 64×64 is the on-card display zone, not the source size | MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E size clarification |

### Boundary with MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E

`MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` (“Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card”)
owns the CSV→sprite mapping, the resolver, the regeneration tooling and the
pending-aware drift guard. **This item is the art-production/delivery item**:
the producer supplies the remaining source sprites; this item commits them and
regenerates the map and static SVGs. This boundary is already recorded in
`tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts`, which names `MS-0MTSAWSME004BH6S` as the
art-production item.

### Remaining work (producer-owned)

45 sprite targets are still pending, listed in
`tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` (`PENDING_ART_TARGETS`) and in the
“Remaining art brief” comment on MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E:

- 24 staff sprites (one per role, per producer decision Q5),
- 12 event-category sprites (`Incident__*`, `Investment__*`; bespoke per category, per Q6),
- 9 business/community-space gaps: `Cafe`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`, `Public Art`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`.

Integration steps once `src/sprites/<Target>_1024_x_1024.png` land:

1. `node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` (regenerates `src/card-art-map.json`).
2. Regenerate the static card SVGs (`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`).
3. Tighten the drift guard in `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` to a strict
   zero-`Fallback` assertion (`PENDING_ART_TARGETS` → empty,
   `BASELINE_UNRESOLVED_CARDS` → 0).
4. Update `public/assets/CREDITS.md` with the new-art provenance.
5. Run `npm run build` and the full test suite.

### Plan decision

Auto-complete: the item is not an epic, its acceptance criteria are measurable
and the implementation sketch is present. The mechanism is delivered and the
only outstanding input is producer-supplied art, so no child work items were
created — a decomposition would duplicate MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E. **Assumption:**
the original acceptance-criteria paths/sizes are read as the producer-approved
architecture above; the original ACs are retained verbatim to preserve intent.

## Appendix: Plan session (2026-09-29)

- No new interview questions were required; every open question was already
  answered by existing records:
  - Image format / creation / scope / placement — answered (producer, this
    item's intake Appendix above).
  - Art-production ownership — answered (producer, MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E Q2:
    “I will produce them”).
  - Source-art size and naming — answered (producer, MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E Q4).
  - Staff art granularity — answered (producer, MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E Q5: one
    sprite per role).
  - Event-category art — answered (producer, MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E Q6: bespoke
    per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category).
- OPEN QUESTION (to producer): none blocking. The pending-sprite commitment
  location is settled by `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts`, which records
  MS-0MTSAWSME004BH6S as the art-production item.

# Intake Brief — Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects (MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M)

The `staff-it` (IT Specialist) and `staff-delivery` (Delivery Driver) descriptions advertise coin-cost reductions that no engine path applies. They were rescaled to the ×100 integer economy in `CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC` but deliberately left unimplemented there (Q4 decision), because their wording named a per-business target that has no implementing mechanic. This item decides the intended scope (street-wide, confirmed by the producer) and implements both effects end-to-end.

## Problem statement

The two cards promise a discount the engine never applies, so the printed ability is not the ability the player gets. This item removes that text/data gap by backing each description with a data column and an engine consumer, and by extending the staff cost-text regression guard so the gap cannot silently return.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — reads a staff card's printed ability and expects the advertised reduction to apply where the engine charges the cost.
- **Game designer / balancer** — needs every staff cost-reduction description backed by a `card-data.csv` data column so economy tuning is trustworthy.
- **Developer / QA** — needs the regression guard to fail loudly if a staff cost-reduction description is not backed by data.

### User stories

- As a player, when I employ the IT Specialist I pay 100 less when I refresh the market.
- As a player, when I employ the Delivery Driver I pay 50 less when I buy a business card.
- As a designer, every staff cost-reduction description is backed by a data column and an engine consumer.
- As a developer, the guard fails with the offending card id if a description and its data column drift apart.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **IT Specialist refresh discount is implemented and data-backed.** `src/card-data.csv` sets `refreshCostDiscount = 100` for `staff-it` and its description reads street-wide (e.g. "Modernizes operations. Reduces market refresh cost by 100."). With a hired IT Specialist, `refreshMarketCost(state)` equals `REFRESH_MARKET_COST - 100`; with an IT Specialist **and** an Accountant it equals `- 200`; the result is floored at 0. Verified by unit tests.
2. **Delivery Driver purchase discount is implemented and data-backed.** A new `purchaseCostDiscount` staff field and `card-data.csv` column carry `50` for `staff-delivery`; the parser populates it onto `StaffCard`; its description reads street-wide (e.g. "Handles the logistics. Reduces business card purchase cost by 50."). While a Delivery Driver is hired, the coin cost of acquiring/placing a business or community-space card is reduced by 50 through **all** acquisition paths — `purchaseBusiness` (click, listed cost), `buyAndPlaceBusiness` (drag: discount the base cost **then** apply the +50% premium), and `playBusinessFromHand` (deferred listed payment, including the same-week composite premium) — while `moveToHand` (0 coins) is unaffected. Effective cost is floored at 0; multiple `purchaseCostDiscount` staff stack additively. Verified by unit tests.
3. **Regression guard extended.** `tests/main-street/staff-cost-text-data-consistency.test.ts` registers `staff-it` with `column: 'refreshCostDiscount'` and `staff-delivery` with `column: 'purchaseCostDiscount'` (both non-null, `UNIMPLEMENTED_NOTE` removed), and the description-amount == data-column assertions pass.
4. **New column is schema-coordinated (cross-repo).** The `purchaseCostDiscount` column is added to core `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` (`CsvRow`, `CSV_COLUMNS`, `NUMERIC_COLUMNS`), to the `card-data.csv` header (immediately after `upgradeCostDiscount`, before `art_notes`), to the staff parser, and the `tce-main-street` `./core` submodule pin is bumped; `balance-cards-csv-pipeline.test.ts` column-count/order assertions are updated and pass.
5. **AI affordability parity.** `MainStreetAiStrategy` uses the effective (discounted) business-purchase cost for its affordability/value scoring, so AI play is not disadvantaged. Verified by a unit test.
6. **Documentation updated.** `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (ability/description/rationale cells) removes the "description-only — effect not implemented (gap)" notes and reflects the implemented mechanics; `docs/main-street/specialization-skills.md` records the implemented cost-reduction mechanics. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Determinism preserved.** No new RNG consumption; headless/AI parity and seeded determinism are unchanged. Verified by the existing determinism tests plus any new tests.
8. **Tests, build and full suite green.** New/updated unit tests pass, `npm run build` succeeds, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Source of truth is `card-data.csv`.** Do not hand-rebalance unrelated values.
- **Scoping is street-wide (confirmed).** `refreshCostDiscount` is already summed street-wide by `refreshMarketCost`; `purchaseCostDiscount` is summed street-wide across hired staff (`state.staffCards`), matching `refreshCostDiscount` and the Negotiator skill. Do not silently make either effect per-business.
- **Pricing precedence.** For the discounted +50% buy-and-place composite, discount the listed base cost first, then apply the premium (the rule established by `CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC`).
- **CSV schema addition is cross-repo.** A new column requires a core (`Tableau-Card-Engine`) `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` change plus a `tce-main-street` `./core` submodule pin bump, mirroring the `upgradeCostDiscount` precedent (`MS-0MULW540X009EP9A`).
- **No new RNG consumption; determinism and headless/AI parity preserved.**
- **Minimal churn** — touch only the staff/economy paths in scope.

### Out of scope

- Rebalancing any other coin/reputation value.
- Implementing the other nominal applicant perks (Barista, Bookkeeper, Customer Service Rep, Security Guard, etc.) — their live effects come from the random specialization-skill system (`CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK`).
- Changing the base `REFRESH_MARKET_COST` or introducing escalating re-roll pricing (tracked separately in `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`).

## Existing state

- `staff-it` (`src/card-data.csv`): `cost=800`, `tier=4`, `ongoingCost=100`, `allowedBusinessTypes=Commerce|Entertainment|Service`, description "Modernizes operations. Reduces this business refresh cost by 100." — **no** `refreshCostDiscount` value.
- `staff-delivery` (`src/card-data.csv`): `cost=300`, `tier=2`, `ongoingCost=50`, `allowedBusinessTypes=Food|Commerce`, description "Handles the logistics. Reduces business card purchase cost by 50 for this business." — no matching data column exists.
- `refreshMarketCost(state)` (`src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`) is a single global re-roll of the one-row market (`REFRESH_MARKET_COST = 500`); it sums every hired staff card's `refreshCostDiscount` (street-wide) plus the Negotiator skill (`skill-negotiator`, −100) and clamps at 0. There is **no per-business refresh**.
- `purchaseBusiness` (click, listed cost), `buyAndPlaceBusiness` (drag, `Math.ceil(cost * 1.5 * 2) / 2`), and `playBusinessFromHand` (deferred listed cost, optional premium) charge `card.cost` directly; there is no purchase-cost-discount field or path. `moveToHand` costs 0 coins.
- `computeUpgradeCostDiscount(state, slotIndex)` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`) is the established per-business discount helper (Financial Advisor `upgradeCostDiscount`), applied in the upgrade acquisition paths.
- `tests/main-street/staff-cost-text-data-consistency.test.ts` currently registers both cards with `column: null` and `UNIMPLEMENTED_NOTE`.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` marks both cards "description-only — effect not implemented (gap)".

## Desired change

- Set `refreshCostDiscount = 100` on `staff-it` in `card-data.csv`; reword its description to street-wide wording. No engine change is required — `refreshMarketCost` already consumes the column.
- Add a `purchaseCostDiscount` staff field, `card-data.csv` column and parser support; set `50` on `staff-delivery`; reword its description to street-wide wording.
- Add a pure `computePurchaseCostDiscount(state)` helper in `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` (street-wide sum over `state.staffCards`, clamped at 0) and apply the effective cost in `canPurchaseBusiness`/`purchaseBusiness`, `buyAndPlaceBusiness`, and `playBusinessFromHand` (discount the base cost before any premium).
- Update `MainStreetAiStrategy` to score/afford business purchases using the discounted cost.
- Add/extend unit tests for both effects (click, drag, deferred play-from-hand, stacking, clamp, discount-then-premium, AI parity), and extend the regression guard to non-null column contracts for both cards.
- Coordinate the new column across the game CSV and core balance-cards schema; bump the `./core` pin.
- Update `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and `docs/main-street/specialization-skills.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — `staff-it` gains `refreshCostDiscount=100`; `staff-delivery` gains `purchaseCostDiscount=50`; both descriptions reworded street-wide.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — add `readonly purchaseCostDiscount?: number` to `StaffCard`.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — parse the `purchaseCostDiscount` staff column into templates.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — add pure `computePurchaseCostDiscount(state)` (mirrors `refreshCostDiscount` aggregation/floor semantics).
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — `refreshMarketCost` (no logic change expected for the IT Specialist).
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — apply the purchase discount in `canPurchaseBusiness` / `purchaseBusiness`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketHand.ts` — apply the discount in `playBusinessFromHand` (base before premium).
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — apply the discount in `buyAndPlaceBusiness` (base before premium).
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — use the effective (discounted) business-purchase cost for affordability/value scoring.
- `core/src/balance-cards/csv.ts` — add `purchaseCostDiscount` to `CsvRow` / `CSV_COLUMNS` / `NUMERIC_COLUMNS` (core repo), then bump the `./core` pin.
- `tests/main-street/staff-cost-text-data-consistency.test.ts` — non-null `column` contracts for both cards; drop `UNIMPLEMENTED_NOTE`.
- `tests/main-street/` — new/updated tests for both effects (click + drag + deferred play-from-hand, stacking, clamp, discount-then-premium, AI parity).
- `tests/main-street/balance-cards-csv-pipeline.test.ts` — update column-count/order assertions.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — update the staff ability/description/rationale cells and remove the "gap" notes.
- `docs/main-street/specialization-skills.md` — note the implemented cost-reduction mechanics.

## Related work

- **CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC** (core, in_review) — Staff effects adjusted for the ×100 coin values; Q4 deferred IT Specialist / Delivery Driver implementation and corrected their text only. This item is the explicit follow-up.
- **MS-0MULW540X009EP9A** (completed) — CSV schema: add `upgradeCostDiscount` column; the cross-repo precedent for adding a staff discount column.
- **MS-0MULWC8CR0011NOX** (completed) — Financial Advisor end-to-end: per-business discount helper and all upgrade acquisition paths.
- **MS-0MULWEEE8007J2TB** (completed) — Accountant `refreshCostDiscount` fixed to ×100; the refresh-discount precedent.
- **MS-0MULWBSF9000Z64Z** (completed) — staff description text ×100 consistency; created the guard this item extends.
- **MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ** (open) — "Reroll to cost more": changes `refreshMarketCost` semantics (escalating base) and interacts with the IT Specialist refresh discount. Coordinate if both land together.
- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0** (in-progress) — sibling staff-ability implementation touching the same CSV, catalog and guard; sequence to avoid merge conflicts.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: cross-repo schema desynchronisation** if the new column is added without the core `csv.ts` + submodule pin update. Mitigation: one coordinated change, per `MS-0MULW540X009EP9A`.
- **Risk: scoping leak / bypass.** If the purchase discount is applied only to click+drag, a player could bypass it by moving a card to hand and playing it later. Mitigation: apply it consistently across `purchaseBusiness`, `buyAndPlaceBusiness` and `playBusinessFromHand`; assert the scope boundary in tests.
- **Risk: drag-premium ordering** changes the price. Mitigation: discount the base cost, then apply the premium, and assert in tests.
- **Risk: AI ignores the discount.** Mitigation: update `MainStreetAiStrategy` affordability/value to use the effective cost.
- **Risk: scope creep.** Keep to these two cards only.
- **Risk: ordering conflict with `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`** (escalating re-roll). Mitigation: coordinate sequencing; the IT discount applies to whatever the escalated base cost is.
- **Assumption:** multiple `purchaseCostDiscount` staff stack additively and clamp at 0, mirroring `refreshCostDiscount` / `upgradeCostDiscount`. (Confirmed street-wide.)
- **Assumption:** the description amounts (100 / 50) are correct on the ×100 scale and are not rebalanced here.
- **Assumption:** `playBusinessFromHand` is included in the Delivery Driver scope (deferred payment for a business card is economically a purchase); `moveToHand` costs 0 coins and is excluded. This closes the move-to-hand bypass. Documented for the implementer; the producer may narrow it if desired.

## Design decisions (confirmed)

- **IT Specialist — street-wide refresh discount (option a).** Reuse `refreshCostDiscount = 100` on `staff-it`; reword the description to remove "this business". No new engine surface.
- **Delivery Driver — street-wide purchase discount (option a).** Add `purchaseCostDiscount = 50`, applied street-wide to business/community-space purchases (click + drag, base-then-premium, plus deferred play-from-hand for consistency); reword the description.
- **Description/catalog/guard/schema (option a).** Reword both descriptions to street-wide, back both with data columns, and coordinate the new column across game + core.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (IT Specialist, prior session): "Reuse `refreshCostDiscount = 100` on `staff-it` (street-wide; stacks with Accountant/Negotiator) and reword, or introduce a new per-business refresh mechanic?" — **Answer (producer, interactive): "(1) A — reuse `refreshCostDiscount = 100`, street-wide."** Source: interactive reply in this session. Research: `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` `refreshMarketCost` sums `refreshCostDiscount` street-wide; `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` has `computeRefreshCostDiscount` (Negotiator −100); `staff-accountant` already uses `refreshCostDiscount=100`; parent `CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC` Q4.
- Q2 (Delivery Driver, prior session): "Add `purchaseCostDiscount = 50` applied street-wide to business/community-space purchases (click + drag, base-then-premium) and reword, or scope to adjacency, or leave unimplemented?" — **Answer (producer, interactive): "(2) a — add `purchaseCostDiscount = 50`, street-wide, click + drag, base-then-premium."** Source: interactive reply. Research: no `purchaseCostDiscount` reference exists in `src/` or `tests/`; `purchaseBusiness`/`buyAndPlaceBusiness`/`playBusinessFromHand` charge `card.cost` directly; parent `CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC` Q4.
- Q3 (description/catalog/guard/schema, prior session): "Reword to street-wide, back both descriptions with columns, and coordinate the new column across game + core?" — **Answer (producer, interactive): "(3) a — reword to street-wide, back both descriptions with data columns, coordinate the new column across game + core."** Source: interactive reply. Research: the guard currently registers both cards with `column: null` + `UNIMPLEMENTED_NOTE`; adding a CSV column requires core `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` + `./core` pin coordination (precedent `MS-0MULW540X009EP9A`).
- Prior context (parent, `CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC` Q4): IT Specialist and Delivery Driver were deferred from the ×100 migration because their per-business target had no implementing mechanic; their descriptions were rescaled but their effects left unimplemented. This item closes that gap under the street-wide decisions above.

# Storyline Coverage Analytics in Monte Carlo Harness

## Problem Statement

The Monte Carlo balance harness (MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts) currently tracks card ownership, market offers, and economy history across simulation runs, but has no visibility into storyline event coverage. Storyline events — which form branching chains with accept/reject choices — are a key game mechanic, yet the harness cannot report how often storylines fire, how deeply their chains progress, whether cycles appear, or what impact storyline choices have on win rates. This leaves the balance team blind to storyline-related balance issues.

## Users

- **Balance team / game designers**: Want to understand whether storylines are contributing positively to the game (e.g., do "Accept" choices correlate with higher win rates? Do certain storylines trigger too or too rarely?).
- **Content designers**: Want to verify that all storylines are being exercised in simulation and that chains progress reasonably (not dead-ending too quickly or cycling excessively).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Storyline fire frequency**: The harness reports how many runs and what percentage feature each storyline (`storyline-economy`, `storyline-health`, `storyline-labor`, `storyline-restaurant`, `storyline-tax`), derived from event-choice transcript records captured during simulation runs.

2. **Chain depth tracking**: For each storyline event encountered, the harness tracks how far the chain progresses (number of consecutive chain cards pushed), reported per storyline as a distribution (mean, median, max depth) across runs.

3. **Cycle detection**: The harness detects and counts cycle occurrences (tax → tax-error → tax-inquiry → tax, per `storyline-manifest.json` edges with `cycle: true`), reporting cycle frequency per storyline and per run.

4. **Win-rate impact of choices**: For each storyline with choices (flu-outbreak, popular-menu, recession, strike-service, tax, tax-error, tax-inquiry), the harness computes the win-rate differential between "Accept" and "Reject" choices — similar to existing M2 win-rate delta pattern.

5. **Integration with existing analytics**: Storyline analytics are exposed as new functions in the balance engine (`src/scripts/balance/engine/`) following the same pattern as existing metrics (G1–G8, M1–M7), with graceful degradation when storyline data is absent.

## Constraints

- **Non-blocking**: This is a deferred enhancement; it must not change existing Monte Carlo harness behaviour (strategies, termination, output format for non-storyline fields).
- **Graceful degradation**: All new storyline metrics return `null` when event-choice data is not available in run summaries (consistent with existing M4/M6/G4/G6/G7 patterns).
- **Builds on existing transcript recording**: The harness already has a lazy `recordMainStreetEvent` call path via `require('./MainStreetTranscript')`; the extension should extend this path to capture event-choice data into a new field on `MonteCarloRunSummary`.
- **No UI changes required**: Output is analytical (JSON/CSV), consistent with existing harness output.

## Existing State

- Monte Carlo harness (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`) runs simulations with strategies (market-greedy, demo-greedy, greedy, banking-greedy, random) and records `MonteCarloRunSummary` per seed.
- The harness already records `cardsOwned`, `marketOffers`, and `economyHistory` on run summaries (Phase 1 data).
- Storyline events with choices are resolved in-engine; `recordStorylineResolution` in `MainStreetStoryline.ts` emits `event-choice` transcript events.
- The Monte Carlo harness has a try/catch wrapper for `recordMainStreetEvent` that silently ignores failures when no recorder is wired.
- Storyline manifest (`docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`) defines 5 storylines, 14 edge transitions, and 1 cycle group.
- Balance engine (`src/scripts/balance/engine/`) has 8 global metrics (G1–G8) and 7 card metrics (M1–M7) with graceful degradation patterns.

## Desired Change

1. **Extend `MonteCarloRunSummary`** with a new field capturing event choices encountered during a run (event ID, choice made, chain depth at that point).
2. **Wire transcript recording** in the Monte Carlo harness so that event-choice events are captured (not just ai-action events).
3. **Add storyline analytics functions** to the balance engine:
   - `computeStorylineFireFrequency(runs)`: percentage of runs per storyline.
   - `computeChainDepthStats(runs)`: depth distribution per storyline.
   - `computeCycleStats(runs)`: cycle frequency per storyline and per run.
   - `computeChoiceWinRateDelta(runs, eventId)`: win-rate difference between Accept vs Reject.
4. **Export storyline metrics** from the balance engine barrel file.
5. **Add tests** covering all new analytics functions.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Extend `MonteCarloRunSummary` interface; wire transcript recording for event-choice events.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/index.ts` — Barrel file for new storyline metrics exports.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/storyline-metrics.ts` (new) — New analytics module for storyline-specific metrics.
- `tests/main-street/balance/storyline-metrics.test.ts` (new) — Tests for storyline analytics functions.
- `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` — Reference for storyline definitions and cycle edges (read-only).

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** — write storylines (epic, completed): The parent epic that shipped the storyline system.
- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** — Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema (completed): Provides the manifest data model.
- **MS-0MUMP96XH002SJ89** — Named storylines, outcome feedback & continuity indicator (completed): Provides storyline naming and feedback mechanics.
- **MS-0MUMP944B009PEO6** — Static validator & npm gate (completed): Validates storyline integrity.

# Problem Statement

When using the developer cheat menu (Market Card Cheat) to replace a card in the market slot, the replacement card cannot be taken — the HUD shows "No affordable cards" and the card is not interactive.

# Users

- **Developer testers**: The cheat menu is a development/debugging tool used by the development team to test game scenarios quickly.

**User story**: As a developer tester, I want to add any card to the market via the cheat menu and immediately be able to take/buy that card, so that I can test game scenarios without being blocked by the card being unresponsive.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. **Cheat-placed cards are clickable**: After using the Market Card Cheat menu to replace a market slot with a card, clicking the card successfully moves it to the player's hand (no unresponsive card).
2. **Cheat card appears in affordability summary**: The card appears in the "Can buy:" HUD summary (e.g., "Can buy: 1 business") alongside other affordable cards of the same family.
3. **All card families work**: The fix works for all card families supported by the cheat menu (business, community-space, event, upgrade, staff).
4. **Existing cheat functionality preserved**: Filtering, searching, and replacing market cards continue to work as before.

# Constraints

- The fix must be surgical — only modify the `cheatReplaceMarketCard` function in `MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`.
- Cheat-generated cards already have unique IDs (`${templateId}--cheat-${nonce}`) and reset properties (level, incomeBonus, etc.) — `family` should follow the same explicit-set pattern.
- The fix must not affect production gameplay — the cheat menu is strictly a dev/debug tool.

# Existing state

- **Card templates** in `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` are typed as `Omit<BusinessCard, 'family' | 'level' | 'incomeBonus' | 'synergyRangeBonus' | 'reputationBonus'>[]` — the `family` field is intentionally **omitted** from templates (it is inferred from the array source).
- **`cheatReplaceMarketCard`** in `MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` creates cheat cards by spreading the template:
  ```typescript
  const newCard: AnyCard = { ...(template as any), id: `${baseId}--cheat-${cheatNonce++}` } as AnyCard;
  ```
  The function explicitly resets `level`, `incomeBonus`, etc. for business/community-space cards, but **does not explicitly set `family`** — leaving it as `undefined`.
- **Market rendering** in `MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` determines click handlers by checking `card.family`:
  ```typescript
  if (card.family === 'business' || card.family === 'community-space') {
      s.onBusinessCardClick(card as BusinessCard);
  } else if (card.family === 'upgrade') { ... }
  ```
  When `card.family` is `undefined`, none of these conditions match, so the cheat card is not interactive.
- **Affordability check** in `MainStreetMarketUtils.ts` also filters by family:
  ```typescript
  c => (c.family === 'business' || c.family === 'community-space') && c.cost <= state.resourceBank.coins
  ```
  The `undefined` family fails this check, so the card is not shown as "affordable".

# Desired change

Explicitly set the `family` property on cheat-created cards to match the card's actual family, so that rendering and affordability checks work correctly.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — `cheatReplaceMarketCard` function, where the new card is created (fix location)
- `src/MainStreetMarketUtils.ts` — `getAffordableBusinessCards`, `getAffordableUpgradeCards` (affordability checks that depend on `family`)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — `refreshMarket` (rendering that routes click handlers by `family`)
- `src/debug/MarketCardCheatOverlay.ts` — `MarketCardCheatOverlay` (invokes the cheat function, already passes correct `family`)

# Related work

- **WL-0MUH5HU580064VMR** — "Show which cards are in the current deck in the market cards cheat" (related cheat menu feature, separate work item)

# Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption**: The root cause is the missing `family` field. Verified by code analysis — templates omit `family` and the cheat spread does not set it.
- **Risk**: Minimal scope creep — the fix is a single property assignment in the cheat function.
- **Risk**: If other card properties are also missing from cheat cards (beyond what is already explicitly reset), they may surface later during testing.
- **Risk**: None — no production gameplay impact (cheat menu is dev-only).

# Polish & Handoff

**Headline**: Cheat menu market replacements create cards without a `family` field, making them unclickable and invisible to affordability checks. Fix: explicitly set `family` in `cheatReplaceMarketCard`.

# Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

2. Select any card type (e.g., "Pawn Shop")
3. Replace a market slot
4. Close settings
5. The replaced card is not clickable and the HUD shows "No affordable cards"

## Implementation notes (Map)

### What changed
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — added `StorylineEventRecord` and an optional `storylineEvents` field on `MonteCarloRunSummary`; extracted the shared per-seed loop into `simulateSeed`; wraps each run in a temporary `MainStreetTranscriptRecorder` (restoring the previous recorder afterwards) so the engine's `event-choice` events are captured, then derives enriched records (storyline id + 1-based chain depth + successor) via `deriveStorylineEvents`.
- `src/MainStreetTranscript.ts` — additive `getMainStreetRecorder()` getter (needed to save/restore the recorder; no behaviour change).
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/storyline-metrics.ts` (new) — S1–S4 analytics (fire frequency, chain depth, cycle stats, choice win-rate delta) with graceful `null` degradation.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/index.ts` — barrel exports.
- `docs/main-street/balance-analysis-api.md` — S1–S4 API reference section.
- `tests/main-street/balance/storyline-metrics.test.ts` (new) — 20 tests (unit + harness integration).

### Key decisions / assumptions
1. **Chain depth (AC2)** — defined as the 1-based position of an event within its successor chain (root = 1); a chain continues when an event's base ID equals the successor queued by the previous event of the same storyline, otherwise a fresh chain starts at depth 1. `computeChainDepthStats` reports mean/median/max over the per-event depth distribution grouped by storyline. The plan comment explicitly left this to the implementer.
2. **Cycle detection (AC3)** — a cycle occurrence is a chain transition that revisits a base event ID already seen in the current chain (the shipped tax loop). This is derived purely from the recorded sequence (`successorId` links), so `computeCycleStats` is self-contained and testable.
3. **Choice delta (AC4)** — a run is classified by its **first** recorded choice for the event (a run may revisit an event in a cycle); `value = winRateWhenAccept − winRateWhenReject`, mirroring M2.
4. **Graceful degradation (AC5)** — all four functions return `null` when no run summary carries a `storylineEvents` field; a present-but-empty array yields zeroed results (meaningful: no storylines fired).
5. **Recorder capture** — switched from the lazy `require('./MainStreetTranscript')` pattern to a static import for the recorder setup only. The lazy require silently no-ops under Vitest (and therefore captured nothing), while the existing `ai-action` require path is left untouched. `MainStreetTranscript` has no dependency back on the harness, so no cycle is introduced.
6. **Scope** — no CLI/UI wiring (per the Desired Change); the analytics are library functions consumed by the balance engine. CSV output is unchanged; JSON run summaries gain the `storylineEvents` field (the requested change).

### Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Changed/full unit suite via the test-skill runner: green (~38s).
